title: allOf() returns CF<Void> — must join each, partial results vs fail-all vs fallbacks

s1_definition.profdef: `CompletableFuture.allOf(cf1, cf2, cf3)` returns `CompletableFuture<Void>` — it signals when ALL futures complete but does NOT carry their results (because they may have different types: `CF<String>`, `CF<Integer>`, `CF<BigDecimal>`). You must call `.join()` or `.get()` on EACH individual future to collect results. When one future fails: three strategies: (1) **Fail-all**: `allOf().join()` throws if ANY failed → reject entire operation. (2) **Partial results**: check each future individually with `isCompletedExceptionally()` → return what succeeded, skip failures. (3) **Fallbacks**: chain `.exceptionally(ex -> defaultValue)` on each future BEFORE `allOf()` → all futures always succeed (with real or fallback values).
s1_definition.analogy: `allOf()` = waiting for ALL 3 departments to finish their reports. The "all done" signal (Void) tells you everyone finished but doesn't carry the reports themselves — you must collect each report individually. Department-C failed? Three options: (1) Reject entire batch ("all reports or nothing"). (2) Submit partial ("2 of 3 reports available"). (3) Use last month's report for the failed department (fallback).
s1_definition.oneliner: allOf() = CF<Void> (signal only, no results). Join each CF individually for results. Fail strategy: fail-all (strict), partial (best-effort), or fallback (resilient).
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** `CompletableFuture.allOf(cf1, cf2, cf3)` returns `CompletableFuture<Void>` — it signals when ALL futures complete but does NOT carry their results (because they may have different types: `CF<String>`, `CF<Integer>`, `CF<BigDecimal>`). You must call `.join()` or `.get()` on EACH individual future to collect results. When one future fails: three strategies: (1) **Fail-all**: `allOf().join()` throws if ANY failed → reject entire operation. (2) **Partial results**: check each future individually with `isCompletedExceptionally()` → return what succeeded, skip failures. (3) **Fallbacks**: chain `.exceptionally(ex -> defaultValue)` on each future BEFORE `allOf()` → all futures always succeed (with real or fallback values).

**In simple words (banking analogy):** `allOf()` = waiting for ALL 3 departments to finish their reports. The "all done" signal (Void) tells you everyone finished but doesn't carry the reports themselves — you must collect each report individually. Department-C failed? Three options: (1) Reject entire batch ("all reports or nothing"). (2) Submit partial ("2 of 3 reports available"). (3) Use last month's report for the failed department (fallback).

**One line to remember:** allOf() = CF<Void> (signal only, no results). Join each CF individually for results. Fail strategy: fail-all (strict), partial (best-effort), or fallback (resilient).

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The loan approval dashboard called 3 APIs in parallel via `allOf()`.** Credit bureau occasionally timed out (5% of requests). With fail-all strategy: 5% of dashboard loads showed ERROR even though balance and property data were fine. Fix: fallback strategy — `scoreCF.exceptionally(ex -> cachedScore)`. Credit bureau down → cached score used → dashboard always loads. For the actual loan DECISION: fail-all (strict — all 3 must succeed for approval).

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** 3 CFs started in parallel: balance, score, property. `allOf()` waits for all three.

**Step 2 (fail-all).** Score CF throws → `allOf().join()` throws CompletionException → entire loan application rejected.

**Step 3 (partial).** Score CF throws → `allOf().exceptionally(ex -> null)` swallows → check each CF individually → return balance + property (2 of 3).

**Step 4 (fallback).** Score CF has `.exceptionally(ex -> 500)` → score CF ALWAYS succeeds → allOf completes normally → all 3 results available (real or fallback).
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ allOf() — returns Void, must join each ═══

  allOf(cf1, cf2, cf3).join() → null (Void!)
  cf1.join() → 100000
  cf2.join() → 750          (or throws if failed!)
  cf3.join() → 5000000

  ═══ THREE STRATEGIES WHEN ONE FAILS ═══

  FAIL-ALL:     allOf().join() → CompletionException! Reject everything.
  PARTIAL:      allOf().exceptionally(null) → check each → collect what succeeded.
  FALLBACK:     cf.exceptionally(ex → default) BEFORE allOf → all always succeed!
```

```
  ═══ HLD — Resilient Dashboard with Fallbacks ═══

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Loan Dashboard                                    │
  │                                                    │
  │  CF<Balance> → exceptionally(→ cachedBalance)     │
  │  CF<Score>   → exceptionally(→ cachedScore)       │
  │  CF<Property>→ exceptionally(→ BigDecimal.ZERO)   │
  │                                                    │
  │  allOf(safeBalance, safeScore, safeProperty).join()│
  │  ALL always succeed (real or fallback)!            │
  │  Dashboard ALWAYS loads! (Recommended) │
  │                                                    │

  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — allOf internals ═══

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  CompletableFuture.allOf(cf...)       │
  │  - Creates internal CF<Void>          │
  │  - Completes when ALL input CFs done  │
  │  - If ANY input throws → allOf throws │
  │  - Returns: CF<Void> (no results!)    │
  │  - Must join each input CF for results│
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  CompletableFuture.anyOf(cf...)       │
  │  - Completes when FIRST input CF done │
  │  - Returns: CF<Object> (first result!)│
  │  - Others may still be running        │
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  Fallback pattern:
  CF<T> safe = original.exceptionally(ex -> defaultValue);
  // 'safe' ALWAYS completes normally!
  // Chain BEFORE allOf → allOf never fails!
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
`CompletableFuture.allOf()` returns `CF<Void>` because the input futures may have different types — it can't carry heterogeneous results. It signals "all done" but you must `.join()` each future individually to collect results. When one future fails: three strategies. Fail-all: `allOf().join()` throws → reject entire operation (for strict consistency like loan decisions). Partial results: swallow allOf exception, check each future's `isCompletedExceptionally()`, return what succeeded. Fallbacks: chain `.exceptionally(ex -> default)` on each future BEFORE allOf → all futures always succeed with real or fallback values (best for resilient dashboards).

In banking: loan dashboard loads 3 data sources. Credit bureau down 5% of the time. Fail-all: 5% error rate on dashboard. Fallback: `scoreCF.exceptionally(ex -> cachedScore)` → dashboard always loads with cached score when live score unavailable. For the actual loan APPROVAL: fail-all (all 3 real values required for accurate decision).
